name: draw-line-text
title: Draw Line Text
description: A single word of serif italic text that draws itself in outline letter by letter like handwriting, then fills in solid. It replays and can stagger each letter.
use: A short hero word or brand name should feel handwritten and reveal itself once when the page loads.
avoid: It suits one or two words only; long lines would crawl slowly, and it needs GSAP and a fixed font size.
a11y: The word is plain SVG text, but nothing marks it as a heading or labels the graphic, and the drawing always runs because there is no reduced-motion check. (keyboard: n-a, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: On a black stage, a large white italic serif word sits centred above a small grey caption. Mid-animation the letters read as thin hairline outlines with serif flourishes; once complete they are solid white letterforms with faint shadows.
behaves: On mount the strokes are traced from nothing over a few seconds, letter by letter, then the fill fades in. The demo restarts it every eight and a half seconds, so the word alternates between outline strokes and solid white.
customise: Text, colour, font size, stroke width, letter and word spacing, whether letters draw one by one, and whether to fill after drawing are all props; timing is fixed in the GSAP timeline.
weight: light: A handful of SVG text nodes animated once by a single GSAP timeline.
demo: The word 'Hello' and the caption 'Drawn stroke by stroke, then filled in.'
issues: Frame 1 shows only a fragment of one letter, so the word is unreadable until the draw completes.
The thin outline stage is faint against the black stage.
There is no reduced-motion handling, so the draw always replays.
polishWhy: Elegant serif draw-and-fill; the outline stage is faint and reduced motion is ignored.
